the development of a sustainable SSF in a MPA, which is the main objective of this study.
the development of a management plan for the area, in order to improve the sustainability of the SSF, the conservation and the enhancement of the local marine resources.
the characterization and monitoring of SSF activities, and the identification of conflicts and needs of local fishermen in order to develop an effective management plan for the oncoming MPA.

the study area has to be considered a good example of a small-scale fishery that is in a transition phase towards the development of a sustainable fishery.

the establishment of a Local Fishery Management Plan (LFMP) and a new Marine Protected Area (MPA) could be a useful and necessary step to protect the local marine resources, to improve the management of fishing activities and to reduce the conflict with illegal and recreational fishery.
the SSF of the oncoming Marine Protected area of Cape Milazzo is in a status of suffering, but with the possibility to recover if a correct LMP and MPA management will be implemented.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the study area is characterized by a SSF with a high level of fishing pressure and conflicts with illegal and sport fishing.

the establishment of a MPA should take the local SSF into account in order to develop an adequate management plan, allowing for the maintenance, not only of environmental protection, but also for the social and economic sustainability.

the establishment of a LMP has improved the management of local SSF, but the establishment of the new Marine Protected Area should take into account the local fishermen's needs, as the LMP is not able to solve all the conflicts with illegal fishing.

the implementation of a LMP is a first step for the management of SSF in the oncoming MPA, which will help to improve the knowledge of fish resources and fishing activities, and to reduce the conflicts between artisanal fishermen and illegal fishing.

the establishment of the MPA should take these results into account in order to develop an appropriate management plan, also allowing for maintenance of the biologic, social, and economic sustainability of local fishing activities.
